stem.en:
Dilnoza expected the new puzzle to take her all evening, since it had a thousand pieces. However, its picture was made of a few large areas of bright, clear color, and she finished it in under an hour. The puzzle turned out to be surprisingly ______.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

options.en: easy

expensive
old

why.en: 'However' turns against 'all evening', and she finished in under an hour: the puzzle was 'easy'. 'Difficult' goes the way of her expectation, not against it.
why.uz: «However» «all evening» (butun kech) degan kutishga zidlikni bildiradi: u bir soatga yetmay tugatdi, pazl «easy» (oson) boʻlib chiqdi. «Difficult» esa kutilgan fikrni davom ettiradi, unga zid emas.
why.ru: «However» поворачивает против «all evening», и она справилась меньше чем за час: пазл оказался «easy» (лёгким). «Difficult» идёт в сторону ожидания, а не против него.

stem.en:
The school's report on the new timetable describes its effect on attendance as ______: absences fell slightly in the first term, too little for the authors to be sure that the timetable was the cause.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

options.en: marginal
dramatic
harmful
imaginary

why.en: Absences fell only 'slightly', too little to be sure of the cause: a small effect, 'marginal'. 'Dramatic' is too strong, and absences did fall, so it is not 'imaginary' or 'harmful'.
why.uz: Darsga kelmaslik faqat «slightly» (biroz) kamaydi, sababiga ishonch yoʻq: kichik taʼsir — «marginal». «Dramatic» juda kuchli; kamayish boʻlgani uchun «imaginary» ham emas.
why.ru: Пропусков стало лишь «slightly» меньше, причина не ясна: эффект небольшой — «marginal» (незначительный). «Dramatic» — слишком сильно, а раз пропуски сократились, он не «imaginary».

stem.en:
Our town should keep its Sunday book market in the old square rather than move it to the new shopping center. The square is within walking distance of most homes, its trees shade the stalls in summer, and the market brings customers to the cafés around it. The shopping center does have one advantage, a roof against the rain, but rain falls on only a handful of Sundays a year.

Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

options.en: It states a position, gives reasons for it, and then grants and plays down a point for the other side.
It states a position, gives reasons for it, and then admits that the other choice is in fact the better one.
It describes a book market, then explains why it moved to the new shopping center.
It compares two places, then leaves the choice between them to the reader.

why.en: It argues for the old square with three reasons, then grants the center's one advantage, a roof, and plays it down: rain falls on only a few Sundays. It does not switch sides.
why.uz: Matn eski maydonni uch dalil bilan yoqlaydi, soʻng markazning bitta afzalligini (tom) tan oladi va ahamiyatini kamaytiradi: yomgʻir faqat bir necha yakshanbada yogʻadi. U tomonini oʻzgartirmaydi.
why.ru: Текст отстаивает старую площадь тремя доводами, затем признаёт одно преимущество центра — крышу — и преуменьшает его: дождь лишь в немногие воскресенья. Он не меняет сторону.

stem.en:
When the drama club moved its show from the school hall to the open-air stage in the park, the director expected a smaller audience, since the park is far from most students' homes. Instead, the audience doubled: families out for an evening walk stopped to watch, and many stayed to the end. The club has now booked the park for all of its summer shows.

Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

options.en: It reports a prediction, describes an outcome that went against it, and notes a decision that followed.
It reports a prediction, describes an outcome that confirmed it, and then explains why the club changed its plans.
It describes a play, then explains why families who watched it enjoyed it so much.
It compares two stages, then argues that the school hall is too small for the club.

why.en: The director 'expected a smaller audience'; 'Instead' it doubled, and the club booked the park for the summer. A prediction, an outcome against it, then a decision.
why.uz: Rejissyor kamroq tomoshabin kutgan («expected a smaller audience»); «Instead» ular ikki barobar koʻpaydi, toʻgarak parkni butun yozga band qildi. Taxmin, unga zid natija, keyin qaror.
why.ru: Режиссёр «expected a smaller audience»; «Instead» зрителей стало вдвое больше, и кружок забронировал парк на всё лето. Прогноз, итог, который его опроверг, затем решение.

stem.en:
In everyday speech, a "desert" is any place that is hot and sandy. Geographers use the word differently: for them, a desert is any region that receives very little rain or snow, whatever its temperature. By that definition, some of the largest deserts on Earth are covered not in sand but in ice.

Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

options.en: To contrast two meanings of a word and show a surprising result of one
To argue that geographers should stop using the word "desert" in their work
To describe the plants and animals that live in the icy regions of the Earth
To explain why it rarely rains in places that are both hot and sandy

why.en: The text sets the everyday meaning of 'desert' against the geographers' one, then shows what follows: icy deserts. It contrasts two meanings; it neither argues nor explains rain.
why.uz: Matn «desert» soʻzining kundalik maʼnosini geograflarnikiga qarama-qarshi qoʻyadi va natijasini koʻrsatadi: muzli choʻllar. U ikki maʼnoni solishtiradi, bahslashmaydi.
why.ru: Текст противопоставляет бытовое значение слова «desert» значению у географов и показывает следствие: ледяные пустыни. Он сравнивает два значения, а не спорит.

Everyone at the wedding agreed that Dildora's cake was a masterpiece: five white tiers, each ringed with tiny sugar roses. Guests photographed it, and the bride's mother asked for Dildora's number. Only her younger sister knew that the roses had been made at three in the morning, by her, after Dildora had fallen asleep at the kitchen table.

Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

options.en: It describes a public success, then reveals a hidden contribution behind it.
It describes a public success, then reveals that the cake had been bought.
It describes a wedding, then explains what the sugar roses on cakes mean.
It describes a quarrel between two sisters, then tells how it was finally settled.

why.en: Part 1: everyone praises Dildora's cake. Part 2: 'Only her younger sister knew' that she, the sister, made the roses at night. A public success, then a hidden helper behind it.
why.uz: 1-qism: hamma Dildoraning tortini maqtaydi. 2-qism: «Only her younger sister knew»: atirgullarni tunda singlisi yasagan. Ommaviy muvaffaqiyat, keyin uning ortidagi yashirin yordam.
why.ru: Часть 1: все хвалят торт Дилдоры. Часть 2: «Only her younger sister knew» — розы ночью сделала сестра. Публичный успех, затем скрытая помощь, стоящая за ним.

stem.en:
The proposal to shorten the school lunch break rests on the claim that students waste the extra time. A look at the yard during lunch suggests otherwise: the chess club meets at the corner tables, the choir rehearses in the hall, and older students help younger ones with reading in the library. Shortening the break would cut these activities, not idle time.

Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

options.en: To argue against a proposal by challenging the claim it depends on
To describe the clubs and activities that meet at the school during the lunch break
To argue that the school's lunch break should be made longer
To explain why students need more time to eat their lunch

why.en: The proposal 'rests on the claim' of wasted time; the text shows clubs, choir and reading help filling the break. It attacks that claim; it never asks for a longer break.
why.uz: Taklif vaqt behuda ketadi degan daʼvoga tayanadi («rests on»); matn tanaffusni toʻgarak, xor va oʻqishga yordam toʻldirganini koʻrsatadi. U shu daʼvoni rad etadi.

stem.en:
The following text is from a short story.

Timur had planned the surprise for weeks: the whole class would hide in the dark gym and shout when the coach switched on the lights. On the day, the coach did not switch on the lights. He walked straight through the dark to his office, humming, and shut the door behind him. After a long silence, someone began to laugh, and then the class marched to his door singing.

Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

options.en: It describes a careful plan, shows how it went wrong, and then shows how the characters responded.
It describes a careful plan, then shows how everything worked out exactly as the characters had intended it to.
It describes a coach's daily routine, then explains why he always hums on his way to work.
It describes a class celebration, then lists the students who helped to organize it.

why.en: Part 1: a plan to shout when the lights come on. Part 2: the coach never switches them on. Part 3: after a silence, the class laughs and marches to his door singing.
why.uz: 1-qism: chiroq yonganda baqirish rejasi. 2-qism: murabbiy chiroqni yoqmaydi. 3-qism: jimlikdan soʻng sinf kuladi va qoʻshiq aytib uning eshigiga boradi. Reja, muvaffaqiyatsizlik, javob.
why.ru: Часть 1: план крикнуть, когда включат свет. Часть 2: тренер свет не включает. Часть 3: после тишины класс смеётся и с песней идёт к его двери. План, неудача, реакция.

stem.en:
Is it better to learn a new language through grammar rules or through conversation? Teachers have argued the question for a century, and the answer may depend on the learner. Adults who already know one foreign language often find rules a useful shortcut, while young children, who have no such habit, tend to pick up patterns from talk long before they can name them.

Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

options.en: To suggest that the answer to a long debate may differ from one learner to another
To argue that grammar rules are the best way for anyone to learn a new language
To describe how language teaching has changed over the last hundred years
To show that young children learn foreign languages faster than adults do

why.en: The text asks an old question and answers 'may depend on the learner', then shows rules helping some adults and talk helping young children. It never says who learns faster.
why.uz: Matn eski savolni beradi va «may depend on the learner» deb javob qiladi: baʼzi kattalarga qoidalar, kichik bolalarga esa suhbat yordam beradi. Kim tezroq oʻrganishi aytilmagan.
why.ru: Текст задаёт давний вопрос и отвечает «may depend on the learner»: одним взрослым помогают правила, маленьким детям — разговор. О том, кто учится быстрее, не сказано.

stem.en:
On cold, still mornings, the lake below the village sometimes seems to steam, as if it were boiling. The water is not hot, of course. It is only warmer than the freezing air above it, and the moisture that rises from its surface cools at once into small clouds that drift over the water.

Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

options.en: To explain the real cause of a sight that suggests something else
To argue that the lake is unsafe for swimmers in the winter
To describe what the lake below the village looks like on warm summer mornings
To show that the lake is much hotter than visitors believe

why.en: The lake 'seems to steam, as if it were boiling', but 'The water is not hot': the text explains the real cause, water warmer than the freezing air. It never says the lake is hot.
why.uz: Koʻl «seems to steam, as if it were boiling», lekin «The water is not hot»: matn haqiqiy sababni tushuntiradi: suv ayozli havodan iliqroq. Suv issiq deyilmagan.
why.ru: Озеро «seems to steam, as if it were boiling», но «The water is not hot»: текст объясняет настоящую причину — вода теплее морозного воздуха. Что она горячая, не сказано.

stem.en:
When the school's science club first measured the air in its classrooms, it found that the air was stuffiest in Room 12. The members suspected the old windows. Further measurements, taken lesson by lesson, showed something narrower: the air grew stuffy only during the double mathematics lesson, when forty students from two classes share the room.

Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

options.en: It reports a finding and a first suspicion, then describes measurements that point to a more specific cause.
It reports a finding and a first suspicion, then describes further measurements that fully confirm that first suspicion.
It describes the members of a science club, then lists the projects that each of them chose.
It compares two classrooms, then recommends new windows for both of them.

why.en: Room 12 is stuffiest, and the members blame the windows; further measurements show 'something narrower': only when forty students share it. A more specific cause, not a confirmation.
why.uz: 12-xona eng dim, aʼzolar derazalarni ayblaydi; keyingi oʻlchovlar «something narrower» ni koʻrsatadi: faqat xonada qirq oʻquvchi boʻlganda. Aniqroq sabab, gumonning tasdigʻi emas.
why.ru: В кабинете 12 душнее всего, члены кружка винят окна; новые замеры показывают «something narrower»: только когда в классе сорок учеников. Более точная причина, а не подтверждение.

stem.en:

When our class began each lesson by reading the plan for the day aloud, fewer students asked what came next, and the lessons ran more smoothly.

Text 2
My little brother's kindergarten found the same thing with pictures. When the teacher pinned up drawings of the day's activities in order each morning, the children stopped asking what came next and moved between activities with fewer tears.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the finding in Text 1?

options.en: By noting that a similar result appeared with much younger children
By arguing that reading the plan aloud makes lessons run less smoothly
By suggesting that the class in Text 1 changed for some other reason
By claiming that pictures work better than words for students of every age

why.en: Text 2 finds 'the same thing' in a kindergarten: a plan shown each morning, fewer questions and fewer tears. It is the same idea in a new case, not another cause.
why.uz: 2-matn bogʻchada «the same thing» ni topadi: har tong koʻrsatilgan reja, kamroq savol va kamroq yigʻi. Bu oʻsha fikrning yangi holatdagi misoli, boshqa sabab emas.
why.ru: Text 2 находит «the same thing» в детском саду: план на день каждое утро — меньше вопросов и слёз. Это та же мысль в новом случае, а не другая причина.

stem.en:
Text 1
The school wants to plant a row of pine trees along the sports field, so that players and spectators have shade on hot summer afternoons.

Text 2
Shade would be welcome. But pine trees drop thousands of needles, and the field would need sweeping every week, or the players would slip on them. Whoever plans the trees should plan the sweeping too.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the school's plan in Text 1?

options.en: By welcoming the shade but pointing out work the plan would bring
By arguing that the players do not need any shade during the summer
By claiming that pine trees grow too slowly to give shade for many years
By suggesting that the sports field should be moved inside a building

why.en: Text 2 says 'Shade would be welcome' and then adds the needles: weekly sweeping, or players slip. It accepts the goal and names a cost that Text 1 leaves out.
why.uz: 2-matn «Shade would be welcome» deydi, soʻng qaragʻay ignalarini qoʻshadi: har hafta supurish kerak, aks holda oʻyinchilar sirpanadi. U maqsadni qabul qiladi va qoʻshimcha ishni aytadi.
why.ru: Text 2 говорит «Shade would be welcome», но добавляет про иголки: подметать каждую неделю, иначе игроки поскользнутся. Он принимает цель и называет издержки, которые Text 1 упустил.

This spring, the bakery on Lola Street sold more bread than in any spring before. The owner, Rustam, credits the new sign he hung above the door, painted in bright yellow letters.

Text 2
Sales at the bakery did climb this spring. But in March the city also opened a bus stop right outside its door, and dozens of people now wait there every morning with the smell of fresh bread drifting past them.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to Rustam's explanation in Text 1?

options.en: By pointing to a new bus stop as another possible reason for the rise
By doubting that the bakery really sold more bread this spring than before
By agreeing that the yellow sign alone explains the higher sales
By arguing that the bakery should take down its new yellow sign

why.en: Text 2 grants that 'Sales at the bakery did climb' but notes that a bus stop opened outside in March: another possible cause of the rise than the sign.
why.uz: 2-matn «Sales at the bakery did climb» deb tan oladi, lekin martda eshik oldida avtobus bekati ochilganini aytadi: bu savdo oshishining peshlavhadan boshqa ehtimoliy sababi.
why.ru: Text 2 признаёт: «Sales at the bakery did climb», но отмечает, что в марте у двери открыли остановку: это ещё одна возможная причина роста, помимо вывески.

Our school now lets students listen to music on headphones during silent reading. Most students in my class say it helps them concentrate, and the class's reading marks have gone up this term.

Music may help many readers, but not all of them. My friend Bahor says that any music, even soft music, pulls her attention away from the words; for her, silent reading has to be silent.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the rule described in Text 1?

By arguing that music hurts most readers
By agreeing that music helps every student in the class to concentrate
By claiming that the class's reading marks fell after the rule began

why.en: Text 2 grants that music 'may help many readers, but not all': for Bahor any music pulls her from the words. It limits the rule; it does not say most readers are harmed.
why.uz: 2-matn musiqa «may help many readers, but not all» deydi: Bahorni har qanday musiqa chalgʻitadi. U qoidaga cheklov qoʻyadi, koʻpchilikka zarar qiladi, demaydi.
why.ru: Text 2 признаёт, что музыка «may help many readers, but not all»: Бахор отвлекает любая музыка. Он ограничивает правило, а не говорит, что оно вредит большинству.

Text 1
In Mr. Ergashev's mathematics class, students who explained their answers to a partner before handing in their homework made fewer careless errors than students who worked alone.

Text 2
In the print shop where I work, something similar happens with orders. When one worker reads each order aloud to another before printing, far fewer wedding invitations come out with the wrong date or a misspelled name.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the finding in Text 1?

options.en: By describing a similar effect in a very different setting
By arguing that working alone prevents errors
By suggesting that the students' errors in Text 1 had another cause
By claiming that printing errors matter more than homework errors

why.en: Text 2 sees 'something similar' at work: reading each order aloud to a partner means fewer mistakes. It is the same pattern in a new setting, not another cause.
why.uz: 2-matn ish joyida «something similar» ni koʻradi: har bir buyurtmani sherigiga ovoz chiqarib oʻqish xatoni kamaytiradi. Bu yangi joydagi oʻsha qonuniyat, boshqa sabab emas.
why.ru: Text 2 видит на работе «something similar»: если читать каждый заказ вслух напарнику, ошибок меньше. Это та же закономерность в новой обстановке, а не другая причина.

stem.en:
Text 1
To find out which classroom is coldest in winter, the student council asked every class to vote. Room 4 received the most votes, so the council has asked the school to put a new heater there.

Text 2
A vote measures how students feel, and the students who voted for Room 4 sit right under its drafty window; the rest of the room may be warm. A thermometer in each room for a week would answer the question better than a show of hands.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the council's method in Text 1?

options.en: By arguing that measuring temperatures would be more reliable than a vote
By agreeing that the vote shows clearly that Room 4 is the coldest room in the whole school
By claiming that students feel the cold less than their teachers do
By suggesting that the drafty window in Room 4 should be removed

why.en: Text 2 says a vote shows feelings, shaped here by one drafty window, and that thermometers for a week would answer better: it questions the council's way of finding the coldest room.
why.uz: 2-matn aytadi: ovoz his-tuygʻuni koʻrsatadi, unga shamol kiradigan bitta deraza taʼsir qilgan, bir hafta termometr bilan oʻlchash yaxshiroq javob beradi. U kengashning usuliga shubha qiladi.
why.ru: Text 2 говорит, что голосование показывает ощущения, а на них влияет одно окно со сквозняком; неделя с термометрами ответит лучше. Он сомневается в методе совета.

stem.en:
Text 1
To get more students to eat breakfast, the school plans to open its canteen thirty minutes earlier each morning.

Text 2
The aim is a good one; too many students sit through the first lesson hungry. But most of them do not skip breakfast for lack of a place to eat. Their bus arrives just ten minutes before the first bell, and opening the canteen earlier will not give them a single extra minute.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the school's plan in Text 1?

options.en: By sharing the plan's goal but arguing that it misses the real cause of the problem
By arguing that students who skip breakfast do not feel hungry during the first lesson
By agreeing that opening the canteen earlier will solve the problem
By claiming that the canteen does not serve any breakfast at all

why.en: Text 2 calls the aim 'a good one' but says students skip breakfast because their bus arrives ten minutes before the bell, so an earlier canteen does not touch the real cause.
why.uz: 2-matn maqsadni «a good one» deydi, lekin oʻquvchilar avtobus qoʻngʻiroqdan oʻn daqiqa oldin kelgani uchun nonushta qilmaydi: oshxonani erta ochish asl sababga taʼsir qilmaydi.
why.ru: Text 2 называет цель «a good one», но говорит: ученики не завтракают, потому что автобус приходит за десять минут до звонка; раннее открытие столовой не устраняет настоящую причину.

stem.en:
Text 1
When the residents of one apartment block agreed to sort their waste into three bins, the amount they sent to the city dump fell by nearly half within a year. The city council now wants every household in the city to follow their example.

Text 2
The block's success is real, and it shows what neighbors can do together. But it rested on a caretaker who checked the bins each evening and on a recycling yard a short walk away. Across the city, where most districts have neither, the same rule could leave bins full of mixed waste that no one collects.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the council's plan in Text 1?

options.en: By arguing that conditions behind one block's success may be missing across most of the city
By denying that the block really sent less waste to the dump after it began sorting
By agreeing that the rule will work as well in every district as it did in the block
By claiming that sorting waste into three separate bins is simply too hard for most households to manage

why.en: Text 2 calls the block's success 'real' but says it rested on a caretaker and a nearby yard, which most districts lack: the result may not carry over to the whole city.
why.uz: 2-matn uydagi muvaffaqiyatni «real» deydi, lekin u farrosh va yaqindagi chiqindi qabul punktiga tayanganini, koʻp mahallalarda esa ular yoʻqligini aytadi: natija butun shaharga oʻtmasligi mumkin.
why.ru: Text 2 называет успех дома «real», но говорит, что он держался на дворнике и близком пункте приёма, которых нет в большинстве районов: результат может не повториться по всему городу.

stem.en:

Text 2

By denying that any more students have been coming to the cafés on weekday afternoons than before
By agreeing that free internet is the best way for a café to raise its takings
By arguing that students should study at home rather than in the town's cafés

stem.en:
Text 1
The new bicycle lane on Sayram Street has made cycling safer, the city says: in its first year, only six cyclists were hurt on the lane, while twelve were hurt on the main road that runs beside it.

Text 2
The comparison leaves out how many people ride on each. The main road carries thousands of cyclists a day; the new lane, a few hundred. Six injuries among a few hundred riders may be a worse record than twelve among thousands.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the city's claim in Text 1?

options.en: By arguing that the comparison ignores how many cyclists use each route
By agreeing that six injuries prove that the lane is the safer of the two routes
By claiming that more cyclists were hurt on the lane than the city reported
By suggesting that cyclists should stop using the main road altogether

why.en: Text 2 says the city compares counts without riders: six injuries among a few hundred may be worse than twelve among thousands. It doubts what the numbers show, not the numbers.

why.ru: Text 2 говорит: город сравнивает числа, не учитывая, сколько людей ездит; шесть травм на несколько сотен могут быть хуже двенадцати на тысячи. Он оспаривает вывод, а не цифры.

stem.en:
Text 1
Watching the feeders in the school courtyard all winter, the biology club found that sparrows came most often to the feeders placed near bushes, where they could hide quickly, rather than to those standing in the open.

Text 2

By arguing that sparrows prefer open feeders to those near bushes
By claiming that the stalls in the middle of the aisles sell the most
By suggesting that the club should move its feeders into the open

why.en: Text 2 finds 'Something similar' at the bazaar: shoppers, like the sparrows, stay where they feel sheltered. It carries the finding over to people; it does not dispute it.

stem.en:
Text 1
Learning to cook from video recipes is faster than learning from a cookbook, argues Mrs. Usmonova, a cooking teacher: seeing how thick a batter should be or how a dough is folded teaches in seconds what a page cannot.

Text 2
For skills that must be seen, such as folding dough, a video is hard to beat. But for planning a meal, comparing two recipes or checking an amount while one's hands are covered in flour, a printed page that can be read at a glance serves better than a video that must be paused and rewound.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to Mrs. Usmonova's argument in Text 1?

options.en: By agreeing that video teaches some skills well while arguing that print is better for other tasks
By arguing that a printed cookbook is better than a video for learning each and every skill a cook needs
By agreeing that a video is the best way to learn every part of cooking a meal
By claiming that videos teach dough folding more slowly than a printed page does

why.en: Text 2 grants that video is 'hard to beat' for skills that must be seen, then names tasks where a printed page serves better. It limits the claim; it does not reverse it.
why.uz: 2-matn koʻrish kerak boʻlgan koʻnikmalar uchun video «hard to beat» deb tan oladi, keyin bosma sahifa qulayroq boʻlgan ishlarni sanaydi. U daʼvoni cheklaydi, teskarisini aytmaydi.
why.ru: Text 2 признаёт, что для навыков, которые надо увидеть, видео «hard to beat», но называет дела, где лучше печатная страница. Он ограничивает утверждение, а не переворачивает его.

stem.en:

Students who sit in the front rows of our classes, a teacher noticed, get higher marks than those at the back. She concluded that sitting near the board helps students learn, and she has moved the weakest students to the front.

Text 2

options.en: By suggesting that the link may run the other way from the one she assumes
By denying that students in the front rows get higher marks than those at the back
By agreeing that moving the weakest students forward will surely raise their marks
By arguing that students should not be allowed to choose their own seats in class

why.ru: Text 2 говорит, что старательные ученики сами садятся вперёд, поэтому «Their marks may explain their seats»: связь может идти в обратную сторону. Саму связь он не отрицает.

stem.en:
Text 1
Our river once froze every winter, and children skated on it from December to February. Now the ice rarely forms at all. The cause is the new power station upstream, which warms the river with the water it releases.

Text 2
It is true that the river seldom freezes now; my grandchildren have never skated on it. But winters here have also grown milder, and the snow on the hills melts weeks earlier than it did in my youth. The power station may play a part, but it is not the whole story.

Based on the texts, both authors would most likely agree with which statement?

options.en: The river freezes far less often than it once did.
The power station alone keeps the river from freezing.
Winters near the river are as cold as they used to be.
Children still skate on the river most winters.

why.en: Text 1: 'Now the ice rarely forms'; Text 2: 'the river seldom freezes now'. Both accept that; Text 2 doubts that the power station is 'the whole story'.
why.uz: 1-matn: «Now the ice rarely forms»; 2-matn: «the river seldom freezes now». Ikkalasi buni qabul qiladi; 2-matn esa elektr stansiyasi yagona sabab ekaniga shubha qiladi.
why.ru: Text 1: «Now the ice rarely forms»; Text 2: «the river seldom freezes now». Оба это признают; Text 2 лишь сомневается, что электростанция — единственная причина.

stem.en:
Text 1
The best way to learn a city is on foot. From a bus or a car, a visitor sees only the main roads; walking, she finds the courtyards, the small bakeries and the shortcuts that give a city its character.

Text 2
Our city has just launched an open-top bus tour that stops at the twelve most famous sights. In three hours, a visitor can see the whole center without getting tired.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 1 most likely respond to the tour described in Text 2?

options.en: By arguing that visitors on the bus would miss what gives the city its character
By agreeing that a bus tour is the most complete way for a visitor to see the whole city
By complaining that three hours is far too long for a tour of a city center
By claiming that the twelve famous sights are not worth a visitor's time

why.en: For Text 1, from a bus 'a visitor sees only the main roads' and misses the courtyards and shortcuts. A bus tour of famous sights is that case, so its author would say it misses the city.
why.uz: 1-matn uchun avtobusdan mehmon faqat katta yoʻllarni koʻradi, hovlilar va tor yoʻlaklarni koʻrmaydi. Mashhur joylar boʻylab avtobus sayri aynan shu: muallif u shaharni koʻrsatmaydi, deydi.
why.ru: Для Text 1 из автобуса видны лишь главные улицы, а дворики и короткие пути ускользают. Автобусный тур по знаменитым местам — как раз такой случай, и автор сказал бы, что он упускает город.
